guarantees.claim: When SecMasking is false, sb_in_mask is assigned to all zeros.
When SecMasking is false, prd_masking is assigned to all zeros.
When SecMasking is false, entropy_req_o is driven to 0.
When SecMasking is false, prd_masking_rsd_ack is driven to 0.
When SecMasking is true, sb_in_mask is assigned from state_q share 1.
When SecMasking is true, prd_masking is driven by the aes_prng_masking instance output data_o.
prd_key_expand is always assigned from the high bits of prd_masking using WidthPRDKey.
prd_sub_bytes_d is always assigned from the low bits of prd_masking using WidthPRDData.
When SecMasking is false, prd_sub_bytes_q is a combinational pass-through of prd_sub_bytes_d.

When SecMasking is false, all unused masking-related input ports (entropy_ack_i, entropy_i, force_masks_i, prd_masking_upd, prd_masking_rsd_req, sb_out_mask) are connected to internal dummy nets, preventing floating inputs.

assumptions.claim: When SecMasking is false, the rest of the design does not depend on non-zero masking values; zeros on sb_in_mask and prd_masking are acceptable.
assumptions.risk: If masking is actually required but SecMasking is misconfigured, masking is absent, exposing side-channel information.

assumptions.claim: The aes_prng_masking instance provides fresh random data on data_o upon data_update_i assertion and follows the reseed protocol.
assumptions.risk: If the submodule fails to produce unpredictable masks, the masking scheme is weakened, potentially enabling DPA.

assumptions.claim: prd_masking_upd and prd_masking_rsd_req are driven by external control such that the masking PRNG is updated when fresh mask data is needed.
assumptions.risk: Stale masks could be reused, reducing randomness and compromising side-channel resistance.

assumptions.claim: Parameters WidthPRDMasking, WidthPRDKey, and WidthPRDData are consistent, with WidthPRDMasking = WidthPRDKey + WidthPRDData, and bit-slice widths are legal.
assumptions.risk: Data misalignment or out-of-bounds indexing could corrupt the mask word distribution, causing wrong masks downstream.

assumptions.claim: When SecMasking is true, state_q[1] holds the mask share of the state word, correctly mapped to the Boolean masking scheme.
assumptions.risk: Incorrect share selection could feed the plaintext share instead of the mask into SubBytes, breaking the masking protection.

uncertain_points.claim: The generate block gen_prd_buffer (line 329) is truncated; the full implementation that drives prd_sub_bytes_q when SecMasking is true is missing from this chunk.
uncertain_points.risk: If the missing code lacks proper buffering or contains a bug, prd_sub_bytes_q may not provide the intended delayed mask value, potentially causing a functional or timing fault in the masked path.

uncertain_points.claim: When SecMasking is false, sb_out_mask is tied to an internal dummy net but never used; if sb_out_mask is a module output port, it may be undriven in this mode.
uncertain_points.risk: An undriven output could produce unknown values, confusing downstream logic or causing synthesis warnings.

uncertain_points.claim: The assignment sb_in_mask = state_q[1] when SecMasking is true assumes that state_q is a two-share array and element 1 is the mask share. There is no explicit documentation confirming this share ordering.
uncertain_points.risk: If the masking scheme uses a different share encoding, the wrong share would be used, potentially exposing or corrupting the mask.

uncertain_points.claim: The aes_prng_masking instance is parameterized with SecAllowForcingMasks and SecSkipPRNGReseeding. The security impact depends on the top-level configuration of these parameters.
uncertain_points.risk: If force_masks_i is enabled by configuration, an attacker could force known masks, completely breaking the masking defense.
